meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('yes') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or negation in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Да мне не надо, у меня есть.

examples.text: Да они уже взяли себе.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.

examples.text: Хорошо, что Вика это не видела!

examples.text: Да и хорошо, что ничего нет.

examples.text: Всё хорошо.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('nothing') that declines for case depending on its grammatical function in the sentence.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'seven', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Алло, Саша, у тебя всё нормально?

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'пойти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Лёва, иди за мной, захвати фонарь!

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (root 'хвати'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to flashlight'.
